argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than clean present-tense certification. Aggregate readiness and rehearsal results support the direction of release readiness, but the policy record makes certification supportable only if the current-release packet is treated as conditioned on explicit disclosure of the mortgage servicing subgroup weakness in current documentation before launch. Prior approval and the monitoring comment are contextual support only, not substitutes for current-release documentation. On that reading, the appropriate audit treatment is caveated compliance rather than escalation.
claims_about_business_cost: A full escalation is not required by the admissible record if the audit finding can be narrowed to conditioned certification treatment. The business consequence of escalation is delay to the launch path, while the remaining governance gap is specific and bounded to current-release documentation of a known subgroup limitation.
claims_about_policy: The controlling policy is conditional, not absolute: model-card certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence already identifies the required disclosure subject matter: the mortgage servicing assistant slice is 1.1 percentage points below the warning threshold. The same admissible record also shows what cannot be relied on as substitutes: the prior approval predates the retrieval change and current eval batch, and the release-thread monitoring comment is not reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language. The policy-consistent interpretation is therefore that certification is supportable only as a caveated current-release certification tied to explicit disclosure.
concessions: The current record does not support clean compliance because no admissible evidence shows the updated current-release model card or approved mitigation already exists.
The mortgage servicing subgroup regression is material to a named launch use case and cannot be dismissed by aggregate pass results.
The prior approval and informal monitoring note cannot satisfy the current-release documentation requirement on their own.
